1.question:
What is the name of your new business topic, and how would you describe it? Please provide:

1. **A short topic name** (e.g. "Customer Churn & Retention", "Opal AI Adoption", "Sales Pipeline Health")
2. **A 1–3 sentence description** covering: what this topic tracks or measures, who the primary audience is (e.g. Sales, CS, Product, Finance), and what decisions or actions it is meant to support.
1.answer: Product In-App Behavioral Analytics. Covers: Product In-App Behavioral Analytics, Opal Onboarding

2.question: Which core business concepts should this topic cover? We've pre-selected the concepts most closely related to **Product In-App Behavioral Analytics** and **Opal Onboarding** based on the knowledge graph. Review and adjust before we move on to data sources.

selected.label: Product In-App Behavioral Analytics
selected.description: Captures how users interact with Optimizely's product UI through Segment event data (clicks, page views, audience interactions) and Userflow behavioral journeys.
selected.ai_reasoning: Exact match to the topic name supplied in step 1 — this is the root concept of the domain and already has edges to Segment Event Data and Userflow Data datasets.

selected.label: Opal Onboarding
selected.description: Tracks timestamped onboarding state snapshots, Userflow guided journeys, and raw Segment identify-call events capturing the first contact moment for users entering the Opal experience.
selected.ai_reasoning: Explicitly called out as a sub-domain in the admin's step 1 answer; the graph shows a direct 'informs' edge from Product In-App Behavioral Analytics into this concept.

selected.label: Product Engagement
selected.description: Measures whether paying accounts are actively using subscribed products, classifying them into engaged vs. non-engaged states and tracking the ARR at risk from low engagement.
selected.ai_reasoning: The graph has a direct 'informs' edge from Product In-App Behavioral Analytics to Product Engagement — behavioral signals are the primary input for engagement classification.

selected.label: Feature Adoption Tracking
selected.description: Tracks which specific Optimizely product features each customer account has adopted or has yet to adopt, covering both a positive adoption matrix and a gap (not-adopted) view.
selected.ai_reasoning: Feature-level behavioral signals are a key output of in-app behavioral analytics; this concept also informs Product Engagement, making it a natural companion in this domain.

selected.label: Opal AI Platform Usage
selected.description: Daily usage at product-account and user-account level, fine-grained feature interactions, and thread-volume summaries for the Opal AI platform.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Opal Onboarding sub-domain requires visibility into post-onboarding activation and sustained usage — Opal platform usage data provides that continuity signal.

4.question: Which key metrics and KPIs should the **Product In-App Behavioral Analytics** topic track? We've pre-selected metrics connected to your 5 chosen concepts via `measured-by` graph edges, plus high-signal Opal usage and onboarding metrics computable from your selected datasets. Review, deselect any that don't belong, and define any custom KPIs this domain should own.

selected.label: Analytics - Monthly Engaged Paying Accounts
selected.description: Count of paying Analytics accounts that were actively engaged in the calendar month.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on the Product Engagement concept — the primary headcount KPI for active product adoption across paying accounts.

selected.label: Analytics - Monthly Non Engaged Paying Accounts
selected.description: Count of paying Analytics accounts that were NOT actively engaged in the calendar month.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on Product Engagement — the at-risk counterpart to engaged account count; essential for surfacing disengagement before it becomes churn.

selected.label: Analytics - Engaged ARR - Monthly
selected.description: ARR associated with engaged Analytics accounts in a given month.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on Product Engagement — ARR-weighted engagement translates behavioral signals into revenue health language for executive audiences.

selected.label: Analytics - Engaged ARR%
selected.description: Percentage of total Analytics ARR that is actively engaged.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on Product Engagement — the normalised engagement rate for benchmarking across periods, segments, and product lines.

selected.label: CMP - Core Accounts
selected.description: Accounts classified in the highest active-usage tier of the CMP engagement model.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on Product Engagement — the 'Core' tier is assigned from Segment event data (the foundational dataset for this topic), making it a direct output of in-app behavioral analytics.

selected.label: CMP - Casual Accounts
selected.description: Accounts classified in the mid-range usage tier of the CMP engagement model.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on Product Engagement — one of three behavioral tiers derived from Segment event signals; tracking tier distribution reveals engagement mix health.

selected.label: CMP - Dormant Accounts
selected.description: Accounts with no recorded product activity — the early-warning disengagement signal.
selected.ai_reasoning: Direct `measured-by` edge on both Product Engagement and Customer Churn & Downgrade — dormancy is the critical at-risk behavioral KPI most actionable from this topic's data.

selected.label: Opal - Stickiness (DAU / WAU)
selected.description: Daily active Opal users as a proportion of weekly active users — the short-window stickiness ratio.
selected.ai_reasoning: Computable from DWH_OPAL_DAILY_USER_ACCOUNT_USAGE (selected in step 3) — DAU/WAU is the canonical stickiness KPI for this domain and a key post-onboarding activation health signal.

selected.label: Opal - Stickiness (WAU / MAU)
selected.description: Weekly active users as a proportion of monthly active users — the longer-window stickiness ratio.
selected.ai_reasoning: Computable from DWH_OPAL_DAILY_USER_ACCOUNT_USAGE — pairs with DAU/WAU to provide a full two-horizon stickiness picture, especially relevant for tracking post-onboarding habit formation.

selected.label: Opal - WAU
selected.description: Weekly active users on the Opal platform.
selected.ai_reasoning: Computable from DWH_OPAL_DAILY_USER_ACCOUNT_USAGE — provides the absolute active-user count that feeds stickiness ratios and tracks onboarding-to-activation conversion week over week.

selected.label: Opal - Total Threads
selected.description: Total conversation threads initiated across all Opal users.
selected.ai_reasoning: Derived from the Opal Threads per User dataset (selected in step 3) — thread volume is the primary depth-of-engagement behavioral KPI for the Opal sub-domain.

selected.label: Opal - % of Threads with an Agent Triggered
selected.description: Share of conversation threads in which at least one Opal agent (any type) was invoked.
selected.ai_reasoning: Derived from DWH_OPAL_FINE_GRAINED_USAGE and Opal Agents per Thread (both selected in step 3) — agent-trigger rate is the key feature-adoption depth signal within the Opal behavioral analytics sub-domain.

selected.label: Opal - % of Threads with an OOTB Agent Triggered
selected.description: Share of threads where an Optimizely out-of-the-box agent was invoked (excludes custom agents).
selected.ai_reasoning: Complements the all-agent metric by isolating adoption of platform-shipped agents — a quality adoption signal particularly meaningful during and immediately after onboarding.

selected.label: Opal - Average Credits Consumed — Onboarding Complete accounts
selected.description: Average credit consumption for paid accounts that have reached the 'Onboarding Complete' milestone stage.
selected.ai_reasoning: Computable from Opal Onboarding Snapshots + DWH_OPAL_DAILY_PRODUCT_ACCOUNT_USAGE (both selected in step 3) — measures activation depth at the most important onboarding milestone, directly supporting the Opal Onboarding sub-domain.

selected.label: Opal - Cumulative Users
selected.description: Running total of distinct users who have ever accessed the Opal platform.
selected.ai_reasoning: Tracks top-of-funnel user acquisition into the Opal experience — a leading growth indicator anchored to the Raw Identifies dataset (selected in step 3) that captures first-contact moments.

6.question: What business rules and definitions should the AI know when answering questions in this topic? We've pre-populated the most critical definitions inferred from your dataset, metric, and event selections in steps 2–5. Confirm, edit, or add any rules that are missing.

selected.label: CMP engagement tiers: Core = highest activity; Casual = mid-range; Dormant = zero recorded activity in the measurement period.
selected.description: Defines the three behavioral tiers derived from Segment event signals that underpin CMP engagement classification across the topic.
selected.ai_reasoning: Three CMP tier metrics (Core, Casual, Dormant accounts) were selected in step 4 — the AI requires explicit tier boundaries to assign accounts correctly and avoid treating tiers as an ordered scale with arbitrary thresholds.

selected.label: Analytics engagement (binary): Engaged = ≥1 qualifying Segment event in the calendar month. Non-Engaged = zero qualifying events in the same period.
selected.description: Defines the binary Engaged / Non-Engaged classification used by the four Analytics engagement metrics selected in step 4.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Analytics Monthly Engaged/Non-Engaged Paying Accounts and Engaged ARR metrics were selected in step 4 — without a precise qualifying-event definition the AI cannot reliably filter the Segment Event Data stream to compute them.

selected.label: Opal onboarding stages (ordered): Recently Signed → Kickoff Scheduled → Onboarding Kicked Off → [Onboarding Complete | Stalled Onboarding | Deprioritized Onboarding]. Success milestone = Onboarding Complete.
selected.description: Defines the six stage names, their ordering, and the three terminal states tracked in the Opal Onboarding Snapshots dataset.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Opal Onboarding Snapshots dataset (step 3) and the 'Average Credits — Onboarding Complete' metric (step 4) both reference stage names — the AI needs the stage order and terminal-state topology to compute funnel conversion rates and time-to-milestone correctly.

selected.label: Active user (Opal stickiness): active = ≥1 thread initiated in the window. DAU = calendar day; WAU = rolling 7 days; MAU = rolling 30 days.
selected.description: Provides the precise active-user and window definitions required to compute the DAU/WAU and WAU/MAU stickiness ratios from DWH_OPAL_DAILY_USER_ACCOUNT_USAGE.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both Opal stickiness KPIs selected in step 4 divide two active-user counts — inconsistent window definitions will produce materially different stickiness values and break period-over-period comparisons.

selected.label: Paid Opal account: active, non-expired credit allotment present. EAP and Purple-Button-only accounts excluded from all 'paid' scoped metrics unless explicitly requested.
selected.description: Defines the paid vs non-paid boundary applied to Opal credit consumption, stickiness, and onboarding metrics.
selected.ai_reasoning: Analytics Engaged ARR, per-stage credit metrics, and several utilisation KPIs from step 4 are all scoped to 'paid accounts' — without this boundary the AI may include EAP or free-tier accounts and overstate paid-customer adoption.

selected.label: Source-of-truth hierarchy: Canonical DWH tables (DWH_OPAL_DAILY_PRODUCT_ACCOUNT_USAGE, DWH_OPAL_DAILY_USER_ACCOUNT_USAGE, DWH_OPAL_FINE_GRAINED_USAGE) take precedence over analyst-built views (Opal_Daily_Usage, Opal U Daily Summary). Surface discrepancies; do not silently resolve.
selected.description: Establishes a tie-breaking rule when the canonical DWH grain tables and analyst-built alternatives return different numbers for the same metric.
selected.ai_reasoning: Two ⚠️-flagged analyst-built datasets were retained in step 3 alongside canonical DWH tables — without a documented precedence rule, the AI may alternate between sources across questions and produce inconsistent answers.

selected.label: Exclusions: @optimizely.com accounts and test/sandbox accounts → always exclude from all metrics. Partner accounts (PARTNER_FLAG = TRUE) → exclude from standard reporting unless the query explicitly requests partner data.
selected.description: Defines the three standard exclusion classes applied across every engagement, stickiness, and onboarding metric in this topic.
selected.ai_reasoning: Internal Optimizely users and test accounts generate Segment events and Opal threads that flow through the same datasets as customer data — without explicit exclusions they will inflate engagement counts and onboarding funnels.

selected.label: Opal agent types: OOTB = Optimizely-shipped (Opal OOTB Agents catalog). Custom = customer-created (Custom Agents catalog). '% Threads with OOTB Agent Triggered' excludes custom agents; '% Threads with Agent Triggered' includes all types.
selected.description: Distinguishes the two Opal agent classes and maps each to the correct agent-trigger-rate metric selected in step 4.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both agent-trigger rate KPIs selected in step 4 share similar names but cover different agent scopes — the AI needs the explicit OOTB vs Custom boundary to route questions to the right metric without conflating them.

selected.ai_reasoning: Both Feature Adoption datasets were selected in step 3 — without this rule the AI may treat an account's simultaneous presence in both tables as a contradiction rather than a correct multi-feature adoption state.

The graph carries an explicit `distinct-from` edge between Opal Onboarding and Customer Product Onboarding, and the latter is powered by GS_ONBOARDING_CUSTOMERS, which is not a selected dataset in this topic.

selected.label: "Active user" is context-dependent: Opal context = ≥1 thread initiated in the window (DAU = calendar day; WAU = rolling 7 days; MAU = rolling 30 days, per step 6 rule). selected.description: Both active-user criteria are live in this topic simultaneously. Cross-applying them would produce incorrect stickiness ratios or engagement counts depending on which dataset and window are used.
selected.ai_reasoning: Step 6 explicitly codified two different active-user thresholds, and the Opal stickiness KPIs selected in step 4 (DAU/WAU and WAU/MAU) are only valid if the thread-based Opal definition is consistently applied rather than the Segment-event threshold used for Analytics/CMP.

selected.label: "Segment" in this topic exclusively refers to the Twilio Segment event-tracking platform — the source of Product - Segment Event Data. 8.question:
How should the **Product In-App Behavioral Analytics** topic grow over time?

Choose an expansion policy that governs two things:
1. **Graph depth** — how many hops from your confirmed root concepts the AI is allowed to traverse when suggesting new entities to include.
2. **Trust threshold** — whether AI-generated suggestions are accepted automatically or must be confirmed by a human first.

All three policies apply only to *additions*. Nothing you confirmed in steps 2–7 will ever be removed automatically.

selected.label: Moderate — Depth 2 · Human-confirmed only  ✦ Recommended
selected.description:
The AI traverses up to 2 hops from your 5 confirmed root concepts and surfaces candidate entities for human review. Nothing is added without a human approving it first. This lets the topic grow naturally as the product evolves — for example, picking up a new Opal usage dataset or a new onboarding-stage metric — without requiring a full topic rebuild.

**Best for:** Most teams. Allows meaningful discovery while keeping a human in the loop on every addition.
selected.ai_reasoning: Your confirmed concepts already have significant depth-2 neighbours that may become analytically relevant — Feature Adoption Tracking connects to A/B Experimentation (useful if feature-flag adoption is added to scope), and Opal AI Platform Usage has a `correlates-with` edge to Product ARR Bridge (relevant if the team starts tracking behavioural-to-revenue impact). Requiring human confirmation before accepting any depth-2 entity ensures the business rules and disambiguation pairs from steps 6–7 remain authoritative.
